title: Landing Craft vehicle unloading costs
query: Landing Craft vehicle unloading costs: A LCM(3) (4 MP movement allotment) beached across a not-exposed reef hexside last friendly MPh. At the start of this friendly MPh it unloads its Passenger Sherman. The cost for the Sherman is 1 MP to Start, 4 MP to unload to unload (25% of its MP allotment (FRU) = 13 * 0.25 = 3.25 MP, FRU to 4 MP) and 3 MP to wade in the reef hex (2 MP + 1 MP COT for waterproofed, fully-tracked)  for a total of 8 MP. What is the cost for the LC? Is it 1 MP (25%) to unload, 2 MP (1 MP spent while the Sherman started plus 25% to unload) or 3 MP (the Sherman spent 61.5% of its MP allotment in unloading, and the LC must expend a corresponding percentage of its MP allotment)?

adjudication.rationale: The Candidate AI answer incorrectly states that the cost to unload the Sherman is 1 MP, which is 25% of 4 MP, whereas the Ground Truth ruling specifies that the cost is 3 MP, which is 3/4 of the LC's MP allotment.

generated_answer:
The cost for the LC is 1 MP to unload the Sherman, which is 25% of its MP allotment.

This answer is derived from the rule that states the cost to unload a unit from an LC is 25% of the LC's MP allotment [A23.7-.72]. The LC in question, a LCM(3), has a movement allotment of 4 MP. Therefore, the cost to unload the Sherman is 1 MP, which is 25% of 4 MP.

The user's concern about the Sherman's MP expenditure affecting the LC's cost is not applicable here. The rule for unloading specifies the cost in terms of the LC's MP allotment, not the MP expenditure of the unit being unloaded.

[Source: SR ASL_QA v22.pdf]

This text has changed across versions. Would you like to know how it worked in a specific version, or how it has evolved over time?
ground_truth_answer:
The LCM(3) is a landing craft. I'd say LC rules apply, particularly this one quoted below. This rule does address the aforementioned uncertainty about the 25% MP expenditure. What I don't know is why an LTV4 is being cited here in reference to the question, instead of the data for LCM(3) and landing craft? I guess the unloading procedure could be similar for the lighter vehicles that the LTV4 can carry per chapter G, but it can't carry the Shermans. 

As for the cost, I agree that more than 50% of the total cost of the vehicle to leave the LC is used, but less than 75%, so that would mean 3/4 of the points are spent. I don't think this is staggered incrementally but is totalled up. 

[ EDIT -- USA Vehicle note 51 speaks of MP allotment and movement allotment in the same paragraph. Note that while MF and MP are defined in the index as "measures of movement capability" (no mention of "allotment"), MF allotment is adequately described in A4.11 and MP allotment is not so adequately described in D1.1. There is NO general definition of movement allotment, though it is used in A4.1, D12.5, USA Vehicle Note 51, Korean Vehicle Note 25. We can deduce that movement allotment really means MF allotment or MP allotment, depending on the unit type. IMO "movement allotment" should be added to the Index and defined. ]

12.4 (UN)LOADING: Except as stated otherwise, normal Vehicle—not Boat—(un)loading rules (D6.4-.5; D8.5) apply to LC and their Passengers. A LC Passenger may unload into an enemy-occupied hex. If a LC is Aground (or is Beached across a hexside that is not within its VCA), units may unload from it only into its hex, and do so by expending 25% (FRU) of their MF/MP allotment (plus COT MP if it is a vehicle). There is no D2.14 penalty cost for the presence of the LC in the Location, but Overstacking will apply when a vehicle [EXC: motorcycle] is in the same Location as a LC but is not a Passenger on one. A unit wishing to load onto an Aground LC must be in (or enter, expending that Location's COT to do so—plus, if it is a vehicle, one extra MP for the presence of the LC; D2.14) that LC's Location, then expend 25% (FRU) of its MF/MP allotment (plus, if it is a vehicle, one MP as the LC's COT and one MP to Stop).

title: Does the "No Quarter" declaration allow use Low Crawl to units adjacent to the enemy?
query:
Does the "No Quarter" declaration allow use Low Crawl to units adjacent to the enemy?: Hi all.

As stated in the question, I have a doubt regarding rules A20.21 and A20.3. If one side has declared No Quarter, can an enemy unit use Low Crawl if it is adjacent to that side at the start of its Rout Phase? Or does the prohibition under rule A20.21 still take precedence?

Thanks in advance.

adjudication.rationale: The Candidate AI answer incorrectly concludes that Low Crawl is prohibited due to A20.21, whereas the Ground Truth ruling clarifies that Low Crawl is a form of movement that does not require adjacency to an enemy unit.

generated_answer:
The rule A20.21 prohibits any movement by a unit which is adjacent to an enemy unit at the start of its Rout Phase. However, rule A20.3 allows the prohibition of enemy units from being able to Rally or Rout away from an enemy unit if "No Quarter" has been declared.

Low Crawl is a form of movement, and the prohibition stated in rule A20.21 takes precedence over the option of Low Crawl. Hence, even if "No Quarter" has been declared, units adjacent to an enemy unit cannot use Low Crawl during their Rout Phase as they are still prohibited from moving by A20.21. 

[Source: pdfcoffee.com_asl-2nd-edition-core-rules-pdf-free.pdf | Priority: P1 | Rule: A20.21, A20.3]
ground_truth_answer:
Why are you equating Low Crawl with being ADJACENT????

10.52 LOW CRAWL: Low Crawl is a rout of one Location which requires 
the entire MF allotment of the routing unit (but is still considered a form of 
Assault Movement should the routing unit enter a FFE Blast Area). A rout-
ing unit using Low Crawl cannot be Interdicted. Low Crawl cannot be used 
to enter Marsh or a Water Obstacle, or in any stream unless dry. Low Crawl 
cannot be used to exit an enemy-occupied Location [EXC: Night (E1.54)]. 
All other Rout provisions apply unchanged to Low Crawl, e.g., rout must still 
be towards the nearest woods/building Location within 6 MF.

Nothing in 10.52 requires a unit that wants to Low Crawl be ADJACENT to an enemy unit (Known or otherwise).

A Routing Unit has these options:
* If not subject to possible surrender, it designates its Rout target (nearest woods/building within 6 MF) and:
1) Routs using its 6 MF (3 for Wounded Leader, etc). towards that target; if moving into Open Ground it may be subject to Interdiction (A10.53; A10.531).
2) Declares Low Crawl and only Routs a single hex, AGAIN TOWARDS THE ROUT TARGET.

*If No Quarter has NOT been declared and it begins the Rout phase adjacent to a KEU and cannot Rout in any way to avoid Interdiction, it Surrenders to that adjacent KEU.

*If No Quarter HAS been declared and it begins the Rout phase adjacent to a KEU and cannot Rout in any way to avoid Interdiction, it does NOT Surrender and may either Rout using its 6 MF (taking the Interdiction MC(s)) or Low Crawl one hex and avoiding all Interdiction rolls.

Note that if the broken unit begins the Rout phase adjacent to a KEU, but has a VALID Rout path that does _not_ subject it to Interdiction, it does ** NOT ** Surrender and can Rout via the first bullet above (either using full 6 MF or Low Crawling one hex ... but both still must be towards it's designated Rout target).
